summary: Kazuyoshi Hotta specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo and held positions at Otani University (~2012–2017) and the University of Tokyo Young Buddhist Association.

Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shudo Junior & Senior High School and the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948), and later held posts at Shogen Junior College and Hosen Gakuen College (~1957).
Kazuyoshi Soma (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Meiji Yamada and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University.
Keenan W. Cox specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA at McMaster University (~2012–2014) under supervisor James A. Benn and committee members Mark Rowe and Shayne Clarke.

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (until ~1953). He served as a fellow at the Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study (~1976–1977) and taught at UCLA (~1969–1994).

Kei Kataoka (born 1969) is an Indologist and philosopher who completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo (1992–2001) and studied at National Sanskrit University. He held posts at Tokyo, Wolfson College, Oxford, and Kyushu University (~2008–2013).

Keiichi Miyamoto (born 1948) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1978) under Minoru Hara and served as an assistant professor at Kokugakuin University (~1989–2018).

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied under Kitaro Nishida at Kyoto University (~1921–1924) and held posts at Kyoto University (~1935–1963) and Otani University (~1964–1971).

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Tohoku Fukushi, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He founded Miwa Gakuin (1922) and taught at Tendai Sect, Shukyo, Nihon, Tokyo Higher Normal, Tokyo, and Taisho universities.

Keikyo Nakamikado specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. They have held posts as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University and as a researcher at the Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies.
Keir Magalie Strickland works in Indology and history/archaeology. Strickland earned a PhD at Durham University (~2007–2011) under the supervision of Robin Coningham.
Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kōchi University and Koyasan University.

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1955–1964). He held posts at Sendai College, Rissho University, Hosen Gakuen College, and Tohoku, Tokyo, Kyoto, Kyushu, and Hokkaido universities.

Keith Dowman (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Bhaga Tulku, Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche, and Se Kusho Chomgpel Namgyel.

Keiya Noguchi (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University and held posts at Shuchiin University as professor and Taisho University as director of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism.

Keizaburō Mizuno (1932–2026) was an art historian in Japanese and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955). He held posts at Tokyo National Museum, Tokyo University of the Arts (~1979–1999), and Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art.

Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~2011–2018) under Victor H. Mair and was a visiting predoctoral fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).

Kemu Jin (1912–2000) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Sinology. He held academic positions at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University (~1948–2000).
Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of Florida (~2009–2015), where he studied under Mario Poceski.

Keng Ching works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~2001–2009), later serving as Associate Professor at National Chengchi University (~2010).
